newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: CRICKET-GANGULY POWERS INDIA TO ASIA CUP FINAL.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-GANGULY POWERS INDIA TO ASIA CUP FINAL.

text.p: Opener Saurav Ganguly powered defending champions India into the final of the Asia Cup with an elegant 73 not out off 52 balls against Bangladesh on Thursday.
India will play World Cup champions Sri Lanka in Saturday's climax to the four-team tournament, having edged out qualifying rivals Pakistan.
India, needing to reach their target of 131 in 20 overs or less, cruised to a nine-wicket victory in 15 overs for the loss of captain Sachin Tendulkar.
That took them to second in the league standings ahead of Pakistan, who have never won the Asia Cup, and last-placed Bangladesh.
Man-of-the-match Ganguly, who hit two sixes and eight fours, smashed 78 off eight overs in an unbroken second wicket partnership with former captain Mohammad Azharuddin.
Azharuddin made 23 off 20 balls after India lost Tendulkar for 28 with the total 54 in the seventh over.

Ealier, tight Indian out-cricket restricted Bangladesh to 130 for eight off 43 overs before a shower ended the innings with five of the stipulated 48 overs still to be bowled, overnight rain having already cut the match from 50 overs.
Medium pacer Robin Singh, with three for 13 in nine overs, and leg-spinner Anil Kumble, who took one for 17 in 10 overs, were the major figures in India's economical attack.
